Third, teamwork — cabin crew depend on each other completely, so being reliable to your team is as important as being kind to passengers.

articles.title: 你認為空服員最重要的三項特質是什麼？
sentences: What do you think are the three most important qualities of a flight attendant?

articles.title: 你認為空服員最重要的三項特質是什麼？
sentences: First, composure — staying calm and warm whether it's routine service or a real emergency.
Second, attentiveness — noticing what passengers need before they ask.
Third, teamwork — cabin crew depend on each other completely, so being reliable to your team is as important as being kind to passengers.

articles.title: 用一個詞形容自己，並說明原因。
sentences: Attentive.
I notice what people need before they say it.
At the hotel, I once noticed a pregnant guest looked uncomfortable, so I quietly offered her a back pillow — she was surprised anyone had noticed, and later mentioned that moment in her review.
To me, attentiveness is where great service begins.

articles.title: 面試結束後，如果在路上遇到考官，你會說什麼？
sentences: If you saw the interviewer on the street after the interview, what would you say?

articles.title: 面試結束後，如果在路上遇到考官，你會說什麼？
sentences: I'd smile and greet you naturally: 'Hello!
Thank you again for the interview — it was a valuable experience for me.'
No awkwardness, no over-explaining.
The way we treat people when nothing is at stake shows who we really are, and I'd want to leave the same warm impression off duty as on duty.

articles.title: 華航是否有飛往巴黎？
sentences: China Airlines doesn't currently fly nonstop to Paris.
Our six nonstop European destinations are Amsterdam, Frankfurt, Vienna, London, Rome and Prague.
If a passenger needs to reach Paris, I'd suggest flying nonstop to Amsterdam or Frankfurt and connecting onward with a SkyTeam partner such as Air France or KLM — the journey still connects smoothly.

articles.title: 如果外國旅客問你：華航有飛羅馬嗎？你會怎麼回？
sentences: If a foreign passenger asked whether China Airlines flies to Rome, how would you answer?

articles.title: 如果外國旅客問你：華航有飛羅馬嗎？你會怎麼回？
sentences: Yes!
China Airlines operates direct flights from Taipei to Rome.
Let me check the schedule for you — and if the dates don't fit, I can also suggest connections through our other European gateways.

articles.title: 華航的袋鼠航線是指什麼？
sentences: The Kangaroo Route originally referred to services between Europe and Australia that had to transit through Asia, named for the way the journey hops in stages like a kangaroo.
For China Airlines it means using Taipei as the transit point to link Australia — Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane — with our six European destinations.
Australian passengers can fly China Airlines through Taipei to Europe on a single ticket, which makes Taoyuan a strong stopover point on the Kangaroo Route.

articles.title: 如果旅客問你：華航飛哪裡？你會怎麼介紹？
sentences: If a passenger asked where China Airlines flies, how would you describe the network?

articles.title: 如果旅客問你：華航飛哪裡？你會怎麼介紹？
sentences: I'd find out what the passenger needs before launching into a list — I'd ask which direction they're heading.

China Airlines' network covers Asia, Oceania, Europe and North America: six nonstop European destinations, seven in North America including Phoenix, the newest and the first nonstop from Asia, and Asian coverage across Japan, Korea, Southeast Asia and major cross-strait cities.
Rather than reciting destinations, I'd recommend the route that best suits their purpose, and add that SkyTeam extends the network worldwide.

articles.title: 你是什麼時候決定要當空服員的？
sentences: During my first year at the hotel.
I once helped a foreign guest complete a car rental process that wasn't part of my job at all, and the next day he came back specially to thank me.
In that moment I realised my greatest sense of fulfilment comes from being part of someone else's journey.
That's when I started seriously researching this career — improving my English, studying the airlines — step by step, until today.

articles.title: 你最敬佩的服務業人物是誰？為什麼？
sentences: It's the senior colleague who trained me at the hotel.

She treated every guest as though they were the most important person of her day — even a late-night check-in, even the same question asked for the tenth time, her attentiveness and her smile never dropped.
She taught me that service isn't a procedure; it's the art of keeping people in mind.
I still hold myself to her standard.

articles.title: 面對旅客抱怨或困難，你會怎麼處理？
sentences: First, let the passenger finish speaking — being heard already takes half the heat out of it.

Then apologise sincerely, confirm the core issue, and offer a solution within my authority; if it exceeds my authority, I report to a supervisor immediately rather than leaving the passenger waiting in uncertainty.
At the hotel I handled a complaint from a guest woken by a fire drill, and I resolved it by listening, apologising, then offering a room change plus late checkout — in the end the guest thanked me.

articles.title: 如果航班延誤，旅客越來越焦躁，你會怎麼做？
sentences: If a flight is delayed and passengers grow increasingly restless, what would you do?

articles.title: 如果航班延誤，旅客越來越焦躁，你會怎麼做？
sentences: First, align the information: confirm the latest status with the captain and ground staff so the whole crew says the same thing, because what passengers fear most is that nobody is telling them what's happening.
Second, be proactive: increase cabin checks and offer water and light snacks, spotting needs before the call bell rings.
Third, steady emotions by responding to each anxious passenger with empathy.
To me, a crew that stays uniformly calm is the best reassurance a passenger can have.

articles.title: 最近搭飛機的經驗對你印象最深的是什麼？
sentences: On one delayed flight I was feeling quite anxious, and a ground staff member came over on her own initiative, suggested I download the airline's app to track live updates, and took a moment to reassure me.
That small act turned my unease into trust.
It taught me that what passengers remember often isn't the delay itself, but whether anyone cared how they felt — and that's the kind of service person I want to be.

articles.title: 請簡單用 30 秒左右自我介紹
sentences: Good morning, my name is Shelly Chang.
I work at the front desk of the Hyatt Place, serving international guests every day, which has built the habit of staying steady and attentive under pressure.
I hold a TOEIC score of 795 and TOPIK Level 4 in Korean, and I've lived in both Canada and Korea.
I'd like to bring that cross-cultural service experience into the China Airlines cabin.
Thank you.

articles.title: 請在 30 秒內描述你最喜歡的台灣小吃／運動／節目
sentences: In 30 seconds, describe your favourite Taiwanese street food, sport or TV programme.

articles.title: 請在 30 秒內描述你最喜歡的台灣小吃／運動／節目
sentences: My favourite Taiwanese dish is beef noodle soup.
A good bowl needs broth simmered for hours — it can't be rushed.
That's very much like my idea of good service: what arrives at the table looks like just a bowl of noodles, but behind it is an accumulation of countless details.
Whenever foreign guests ask what they must eat in Taiwan, beef noodle soup is always my first recommendation, because it best represents the care Taiwan puts into things.

articles.title: 如果有下一世，你想變成其他哪個國家的人？
sentences: If you had another life, which country would you want to be from?

articles.title: 如果有下一世，你想變成其他哪個國家的人？
sentences: I'd want to be Korean.
During my exchange semester in Korea I came to appreciate how finely attuned the culture is to reading the room — a lot of care is never spoken aloud, you feel it through actions.
That said, even as a Korean I think I'd still want to fly back to Taiwan, because experiencing another culture is exactly what makes you realise how precious Taiwanese warmth is.

articles.title: 你朋友或家人怎麼形容你？他們會希望你改進什麼？
sentences: How would your friends or family describe you?
What would they want you to improve?

articles.title: 你朋友或家人怎麼形容你？他們會希望你改進什麼？
sentences: They describe me as reliable and unflappable — the phrase they use is that once something is handed to Shelly, they stop worrying about it.
As for what to improve, my family would say I'm too hard on myself; I used to spend far too long reflecting whenever I fell short of my own standard.
Over the past few years I've learned to convert that energy into a concrete improvement plan, and now it's become what keeps me getting better.

articles.title: 遇到身體狀況不適的旅客，你會怎麼協助？
sentences: I'd approach the passenger first to check on them, confirm their symptoms and calm them, so neither they nor the passengers around them panic.
At the same time I'd notify the purser immediately, and if needed make an announcement asking for any medical professionals on board, while preparing the first aid kit and relevant equipment.
After that I'd stay with them and keep monitoring their condition until landing, when we hand over to medical staff on the ground.
The principle is: stay calm, report it, and don't leave the passenger.

articles.title: 有一次你團隊合作成功的經驗？分享經過與學習
sentences: Tell me about a successful teamwork experience — what happened and what did you learn?

articles.title: 有一次你團隊合作成功的經驗？分享經過與學習
sentences: During a holiday peak the hotel was nearly full, and the volume of checkouts meant housekeeping couldn't keep up, so guests began waiting and the atmosphere grew tense.

I first settled the waiting guests and explained the situation, while checking room status directly with housekeeping and asking my supervisor for approval to reassign rooms flexibly, along with late-checkout compensation.
In the end every guest was checked in.
What I learned is that under pressure, communication, coordination and decision-making have to happen simultaneously — and keeping the team's information aligned is the foundation for all of it.

articles.title: 如果面試順序拖延到你精力不夠，你怎麼調整？
sentences: If the interview runs late and your energy is fading, how would you adjust?

articles.title: 如果面試順序拖延到你精力不夠，你怎麼調整？
sentences: I've worked morning, afternoon and night shifts at the hotel, so I'm used to managing my own energy.

While waiting I'd hydrate, do some light stretching, and use deep breathing to stay composed, reminding myself that for the interviewer every candidate is someone they're meeting for the first time — so however late my turn comes, I owe them the same energy as the first candidate.
That's really the daily reality of this job too: however many hours you've flown, you walk into the cabin at your best.

articles.title: 你家人知道你這次考空服嗎？他們怎麼說？
sentences: Does your family know you're interviewing for cabin crew?
What do they say?

articles.title: 你家人知道你這次考空服嗎？他們怎麼說？
sentences: Yes, and they're very supportive.
When I said I wanted to pursue cabin crew, my family encouraged me straight away, and my mother still checks in on how my preparation is going.
As the eldest daughter I've always been independent and someone they don't need to worry about, so they know this is a goal I've planned carefully rather than an impulse.
Having their backing means I can give it everything.

articles.title: 曾經接過哪一次你覺得自己做得最棒的服務？
sentences: I once noticed that a guest checking in was pregnant, though she hadn't mentioned it.
I quietly offered to prepare an extra pillow so she could sleep more comfortably.
She was surprised that anyone had noticed, and later mentioned it specifically in her review.
That confirmed for me that the best service isn't responding to requests — it starts with observation, seeing what someone needs before they have to ask.

articles.title: 曾經你不認同規範或指示，你怎麼處理？
sentences: Have you ever disagreed with a rule or instruction?
How did you handle it?

articles.title: 曾經你不認同規範或指示，你怎麼處理？
sentences: I'd follow the rule first, because rules usually exist for reasons I haven't seen yet — that's the respect for systems my Public Administration training gave me.
If after carrying it out I still felt there was room to improve, I'd raise a specific suggestion with my supervisor at an appropriate moment, describing what I observed and proposing an alternative.
Comply first, suggest afterwards — never question it on the spot or improvise my own version.
In aviation, that's fundamental to safety culture.

articles.title: 請問剛剛念短文時：你覺得講者最想表達什麼重點？
sentences: About the passage you just read aloud — what do you think the speaker most wanted to convey?

articles.title: 請問剛剛念短文時：你覺得講者最想表達什麼重點？
sentences: (Technique) Read actively while you're reading aloud: identify who the subject is, what happens, and whether the tone is positive or negative.

When answering, summarise the main idea in one sentence, then support it with one concrete detail from the text — for example: "The speaker mainly wants to convey how travel makes you grow, and the example of overcoming a language barrier illustrates that best."
Avoid retelling the passage sentence by sentence.

articles.title: 面試結尾如果有機會問我們什麼，你會問什麼？
sentences: At the end of an interview, if you could ask us anything, what would you ask?

articles.title: 面試結尾如果有機會問我們什麼，你會問什麼？
sentences: I'd like to ask: during training, what core capability does the company most want new cabin crew to build first — a solid grasp of safety procedures, service detail, or team coordination?
I'd like to prepare myself in the direction China Airlines expects before I report for duty.

articles.title: 請談談你在凱悅飯店的工作經驗。
sentences: I've been at the front desk for about a year.
Every day is different — one moment I'm checking someone in, and the next I'm helping someone who just had a really long flight and needs things sorted quickly.
I've learned how to read people fast, stay calm when things get busy, and make sure every guest feels taken care of, even during the rush.

articles.title: __QUESTION_BANK__ 95
sentences: We actually have a lot of Korean guests at the hotel, so it comes up more than you'd think.
Being able to speak Korean helps me build a connection quickly — people visibly relax when they realize they can communicate in their own language.
Even a simple exchange can make someone feel so much more comfortable.

articles.title: 韓文TOPIK 4級，有沒有在真實情境中幫到人？
sentences: Your Korean is TOPIK Level 4 — has it helped in a real situation?

articles.title: 韓文TOPIK 4級，有沒有在真實情境中幫到人？
sentences: Yes.
A Korean couple at the hotel were getting frustrated because their room request kept getting lost in translation.
The moment I switched to Korean, the whole atmosphere changed.
It wasn't that I solved it faster — the process was identical.
It was that they suddenly felt someone actually understood them.
That taught me language builds trust in a way that goes beyond the words themselves.

articles.title: __QUESTION_BANK__ 96
sentences: Earlier in my cabin crew journey, I attended an airline interview and wasn't selected.
Instead of focusing on the rejection, I reviewed my performance honestly and found areas to improve — mainly interview structure and speaking confidence.
I kept practicing through my hotel work.
That experience taught me that rejection is just feedback in disguise.

articles.title: 請分享一次失敗的經驗，以及你最大的收穫。
sentences: Early in my hotel job I was handling several check-ins at once and mis-entered a guest's room type, which upset him.
I apologised immediately and worked with my supervisor to prioritise moving him and offer compensation.
Afterwards I built the habit of reading every entry back to confirm it, and that error never recurred.
It taught me being busy is no excuse — the busier you are, the more you need a checking mechanism.
And owning a mistake immediately works far better than explaining it later.

articles.title: __QUESTION_BANK__ 97
sentences: Short term, I want to really master the basics — understand the safety procedures, learn the service flow, and build trust with the team.
Long term, I'd love to use my English and Korean skills to connect with more international passengers.
And eventually, I hope to be the kind of senior crew member who's a steady presence for both passengers and teammates.

articles.title: 未來一年，你希望自己在工作上達成什麼目標？
sentences: Short term, I want to really master the basics — understand the safety procedures, learn the service flow, and build trust with the team.
Long term, I'd love to use my English and Korean skills to connect with more international passengers.
And eventually, I hope to be the kind of senior crew member who's a steady presence for both passengers and teammates.

articles.title: __QUESTION_BANK__ 98
sentences: Yes, fully.
When I told them I was applying, they were supportive right away.
Having that backing makes me feel like I can give this everything I've got.

articles.title: 家人是否支持你從事空服工作？如果反對，你會如何溝通？
sentences: My family has been very supportive.
When I went on exchange in Korea and studied in Canada they encouraged me strongly, and they saw for themselves that I can live independently abroad.
If they had concerns about shift work or overnight layovers, I'd patiently explain the company's safety standards and rest arrangements, and stay in regular contact so they know how I'm doing.
To me, reassuring family isn't about persuading them — it's about letting steady reality do the work.

articles.title: __QUESTION_BANK__ 99
sentences: I'm Shelly.
I spent a year at a Hyatt hotel dealing with international guests every day — check-ins, complaints, everything.
I also studied in Canada and did an exchange in South Korea, where I got to TOPIK Level 4 in Korean.
My colleagues used to call me their go-to person because I pick things up fast and I actually care about the person in front of me.
That's what brought me here.

articles.title: 請自我介紹
sentences: Good morning!
I'm Shelly from Taiwan.
For the past year I've been a front desk agent at a Hyatt hotel, taking care of international guests every day — check-ins, complaints, urgent requests.
I've lived in Canada and studied in Korea, and I speak Mandarin, English and Korean.
My colleagues call me their go-to person because I stay calm and get things done.
Emirates, with crew from over 140 nationalities, is exactly the stage I've been preparing for.

articles.title: 最難忘的服務經驗是什麼？
sentences: An elderly American guest panicked — her Vietnam visa hadn't been approved in time.
Not my job, but I sat with her, helped her through the online process, and arranged for her room to stay at the same rate while she waited.
She came back the next day just to thank me and left a tip.
What stuck with me isn't the tip — it's that she felt taken care of when she had no control.

articles.title: 遇到情緒崩潰的旅客，你怎麼處理？
sentences: A guest once broke down crying at the front desk.
She'd missed her flight that morning and the room issue was simply the last straw.
I didn't jump into solutions — I let her talk and told her I understood how hard her day had been.
Once she'd settled, we set up a sofa bed so she could properly rest, and she left in a completely different state.
It taught me that someone in distress doesn't want a solution first; they want to be caught first.

articles.title: 說說你做過超出職責範圍的事
sentences: Tell me about a time you did something outside your normal responsibilities.

articles.title: 說說你做過超出職責範圍的事
sentences: Housekeeping had clocked out when a guest called about crumbs on his floor.
I'd never used a professional vacuum before, but I went up and figured it out — found the narrow attachment, got the floor clean, left a note for the morning team.
His floor was clean and he felt taken care of.
There's always a way if you're willing to find it.

articles.title: 你在工作中犯過什麼錯？
sentences: Early on I missed confirming a room upgrade for a loyalty member — I wasn't familiar with the system yet.
He'd already checked into the wrong room.
I went to him directly, apologized clearly, sorted it right away, and added a small gesture.
Then I made a personal checklist so it couldn't happen again.
The mistake actually made me more thorough.

articles.title: 有沒有因為說明不完整而引起的客訴？
sentences: Have you had a complaint caused by something not being explained properly?

articles.title: 有沒有因為說明不完整而引起的客訴？
sentences: A high-tier member checked in fast and I didn't walk him through his benefits properly — I gave the welcome gift to his wife instead.
He came back frustrated.
I didn't make excuses.
I apologized and sat down with him to go through everything he was entitled to.
The lesson: fast-moving guests still deserve full service.
It's on me to make that happen.

articles.title: 你有遇過讓你不舒服的旅客嗎？
sentences: Have you ever dealt with a guest who made you personally uncomfortable?

articles.title: 你有遇過讓你不舒服的旅客嗎？
sentences: Yes.
A drunk Korean guest asked for my personal phone number.
I stayed calm — no confrontation.
I told him I couldn't share personal details and gave him the hotel service line instead.
Then I flagged it to his tour guide to keep an eye on him.
The boundary was held without drama.
Staying warm but firm works much better than getting defensive.

articles.title: 工作壓力大你怎麼調適？
sentences: I'm naturally optimistic — most frustrations look much smaller after a night's sleep.
I try to draw a mental line when my shift ends: I did my best, now I reset.
I don't replay things or vent online.
I do note what went wrong so I can improve.
Reset first, then get better.

articles.title: 韓國和加拿大的生活經驗如何影響你和人相處？
sentences: How did living in Korea and Canada shape how you work with people?

articles.title: 韓國和加拿大的生活經驗如何影響你和人相處？
sentences: Living somewhere is different from visiting.
Canada taught me to be direct — people say what they mean and expect the same.
Korea was almost the opposite — a lot is communicated through context and relationship.
What I got from both is flexibility.
I don't assume someone's rude because they're direct, or evasive because they're indirect.
I try to meet people where they are.

articles.title: 旅客對你言語攻擊，你怎麼處理？
sentences: I don't match their energy.
I keep my voice low and steady, give them a bit of space, and focus on what they're actually upset about, not the tone.
Something like: 'I hear you're frustrated — can you help me understand what happened?'
If they continue or disturb others, I'd involve the purser and follow protocol.
But I genuinely try to resolve it first.

articles.title: 旅客說他的特殊餐沒帶上機，但艙單上沒有記錄
sentences: A passenger insists their special meal wasn't loaded, but it's not in the manifest.

articles.title: 旅客說他的特殊餐沒帶上機，但艙單上沒有記錄
sentences: I wouldn't argue about the manifest — that just creates conflict.
I'd acknowledge their frustration, apologize we're in this situation, then focus on what I can actually do.
I'd check what's on board and find the closest option to their needs.
If it's a medical allergy, I'd escalate to the purser immediately.
Either way, I'd document it for follow-up on the ground.

articles.title: 鄰座旅客激烈爭吵，你如何介入？
sentences: I'd approach calmly — not rushing in a way that signals panic.
I'd address them both: 'Excuse me, I just want to make sure everything's okay.'
That gives everyone a moment to pause.
If still heated, I'd offer to reseat one of them — framing it as comfort, not punishment.
I wouldn't take sides.
The goal is the whole cabin, not the dispute itself.

articles.title: 旅客不斷按服務鈴提小要求，影響整體服務
sentences: I wouldn't show frustration — they might just feel unattended to.
When I respond, I'd check in more broadly: 'Is there anything else I can get you while I'm here?'
That often pre-empts the next few requests.
I'd also stop by their seat during natural pauses in service.
Most people aren't being difficult — they just want to feel like someone's paying attention.

articles.title: 你注意到旅客可能有飛行恐懼症，你怎麼做？
sentences: I'd approach quietly — no big scene.
Offer a drink, and while I'm there softly ask if they're doing okay.
If they mention being nervous, I wouldn't minimize it — I'd acknowledge it and maybe tell them what to expect: turbulence, timing.
I'd check in again later too.
It's less about solving the fear and more about making them feel less alone with it.

articles.title: 處理奧客的經驗（STAR）
sentences: Situation: a guest burst into tears at check-in — she'd missed her flight that morning, and the room delay was the last straw.
Task: I needed to calm her and find a solution.
Action: instead of jumping to logistics, I let her talk and acknowledged how hard her day had been; once she settled, I offered a sofa-bed setup since her preferred room type was full.
Result: she accepted gracefully and thanked me at checkout.
It taught me that in service, how you make someone feel often matters more than the fix itself.

articles.title: 超出職責範圍服務的經驗（STAR）
sentences: Tell me about a time you went above and beyond for a customer.

articles.title: 超出職責範圍服務的經驗（STAR）
sentences: Situation: an elderly American guest panicked because her Vietnam visa hadn't been approved in time.
Task: it wasn't my job, but she had no one else to turn to.
Action: I sat with her, walked her through the online process step by step, and arranged for her room rate to stay the same while she waited.
Result: the visa came through, and she returned the next day just to thank me.
What stayed with me is that she felt taken care of at the moment she had no control — that's what service means to me.

articles.title: 請用 STAR 架構分享一次你在工作中犯錯的經驗。
sentences: Tell me about a mistake you made at work.
(Please answer using the STAR format.)

articles.title: 請用 STAR 架構分享一次你在工作中犯錯的經驗。
sentences: Situation: early in my hotel job, I missed confirming a loyalty member's room upgrade because I was still learning the system.
Task: he had already checked into the wrong room, so I had to recover his trust fast.
Action: I apologized directly without excuses, fixed the booking immediately, and arranged a small gesture.
Then I built my own reference checklist.
Result: he left satisfied, and the mistake never happened again.
It made me more thorough — and taught me that owning a mistake quickly beats explaining it.

articles.title: 跨文化合作經驗（STAR）
sentences: Tell me about a time you worked with people from different cultures.

articles.title: 跨文化合作經驗（STAR）
sentences: Situation: during my exchange semester in Korea, I worked on group projects with students from Europe and Southeast Asia.
Task: we had different communication styles — some very direct, some very indirect — and deadlines to meet.
Action: I learned to adjust how I gave feedback to each person and volunteered to be the one aligning everyone's progress.
Result: we delivered every project on time.
Living in both Canada and Korea taught me to read people through their culture, not mine — a skill I now use with hotel guests every day.

articles.title: 與同事意見不合（STAR）
sentences: Tell me about a time you had a disagreement with a colleague.

articles.title: 與同事意見不合（STAR）
sentences: Situation: on a busy evening, a colleague and I disagreed on how to prioritise a wave of check-ins.
Task: we needed one approach quickly, without guests sensing tension between us.
Action: I heard her reasoning out first, then suggested we lay both options in front of the shift leader and committed to backing whichever was chosen.
Result: the queue cleared smoothly and our working relationship actually improved.
What I learned is that the point isn't to win — it's to find the best answer for the guest.

articles.title: 高壓下工作的經驗（STAR）
sentences: Situation: a holiday weekend, the hotel nearly full, and housekeeping running behind — guests were queuing and getting tense.
Task: keep service quality while managing the backlog.
Action: I calmed the queue with clear updates, confirmed live room status with housekeeping, proposed flexible room changes to my manager, and offered late checkouts as compensation.
Result: every guest was roomed and the mood turned around.
Pressure narrows some people; for me it switches on prioritization.

articles.title: 被批評的經驗（STAR）
sentences: Tell me about a time you received criticism.
How did you handle it?

articles.title: 被批評的經驗（STAR）
sentences: Situation: at a previous airline interview, the assessor pointed out that my aviation safety knowledge was weak.
Task: I could either feel discouraged or treat it as a gift.
Action: I thanked them, then built a study plan — cabin safety procedures, emergency equipment, evacuation commands — and started preparing for a first-aid certification.
Result: safety questions are now one of my strengths instead of my gap.
Criticism stings for a minute; what you build from it lasts.

articles.title: 旅客怕飛怎麼辦？
sentences: A passenger is afraid of flying and looks anxious.
What do you do?

articles.title: 旅客怕飛怎麼辦？
sentences: I'd approach quietly — no big scene.
I'd offer a drink and softly ask how they're doing.
If they mention the fear, I wouldn't minimize it; I'd briefly explain what to expect, like normal turbulence sounds, and let them know exactly where to find me.
Then I'd check back during the flight so they know they're not alone.
It's less about fixing the fear and more about being a steady presence beside it.

articles.title: 醉酒旅客還要酒怎麼辦？
sentences: A passenger has had too much to drink and demands more alcohol.

articles.title: 醉酒旅客還要酒怎麼辦？
sentences: I'd stay warm but firm.
I wouldn't embarrass him — I'd offer water or coffee with something to eat first, then politely explain I'm not able to serve more alcohol for now, for his own comfort and safety.
I'd also let the other crew know so we can keep an eye on him together.
I've held this kind of line for real: an intoxicated guest once asked for my personal number and I calmly redirected him to the service line.
That confirmed for me that boundaries work best without drama.

articles.title: 旅客投訴另一位組員怎麼辦？
sentences: First, I'd listen fully and apologize for the experience without blaming my colleague — the passenger needs to feel heard, not to witness a trial.
I'd solve their immediate need myself, then quietly inform the senior crew member so it's handled properly.
Afterward, I'd share the feedback with my colleague privately and constructively.
Protecting the passenger's experience and protecting the team aren't opposites — you do both.

articles.title: 兩位旅客為椅背吵架怎麼辦？
sentences: I'd step in calmly and address both: 'Excuse me — I want to make sure everyone's comfortable.'
That pause alone lowers the temperature.
I'd listen to each side briefly without taking sides, then offer practical options — adjusting recline during meal service, or reseating one of them framed as extra comfort, not punishment.
If it kept escalating, I'd involve the senior crew.
My goal is the whole cabin's atmosphere, not winning the argument.

articles.title: 每班都是不同組員，你怎麼看？
sentences: Emirates crew fly with different colleagues on every flight.
How do you feel about that?

articles.title: 每班都是不同組員，你怎麼看？
sentences: I actually like it.
At the hotel I was paired with different colleagues every shift, so I've learned to sync quickly — confirm who's doing what, communicate clearly, and step in proactively.
Flying with new crew each time also means learning something from someone new on every flight: different techniques, different cultures.
I believe that as long as everyone follows the same SOP the team works, and the variety is what keeps you sharp.

articles.title: 如何應對長程航班與時差？
sentences: How will you cope with long-haul flights, night shifts and jet lag?

articles.title: 如何應對長程航班與時差？
sentences: With systems, not willpower.
I already work rotating shifts at the hotel, including overnights, so I know my body's rules: protect sleep before duty, eat light, stay hydrated, and adjust to destination time quickly.
I do Pilates regularly to keep my energy and posture stable.
I treat rest as part of the job — because showing up at 100% for passengers is the professional standard, not a bonus.

articles.title: 你心中優質的服務是什麼？
sentences: It means noticing before being asked.
At the hotel I once noticed a pregnant guest who hadn't said anything and quietly offered a back pillow — she was surprised anyone saw her need.
That's the standard I hold: make people feel understood, not just served.
On board, with hundreds of passengers from different cultures, that kind of quiet attentiveness is what turns a flight into a memory.

articles.title: 請用3分鐘自我介紹，並結合過去經歷展現你的服務精神與穩定度。
sentences: Please introduce yourself in three minutes, using your past experience to show your service mindset and reliability.

articles.title: 請用3分鐘自我介紹，並結合過去經歷展現你的服務精神與穩定度。
sentences: I'm Shelly Chang, a graduate of National Chi Nan University's Public Administration and Policy program.
During my studies, I took the opportunity to go on exchange in South Korea for a semester and joined a study program in Canada, building independence and cross-cultural communication skills.

After graduation, I worked for almost a year as a front desk agent at Hyatt Hotels, a role that had me facing guests from different countries with different needs every day, teaching me to maintain consistent service quality and a warm attitude even amid busy or unexpected situations.

I also interned at the Xinzhuang Cultural and Arts Center's Performing Arts Division, handling exhibition management, venue administration, and marketing — an experience that showed me stability comes from solid preparation and clear process management.

This year-plus of work experience convinced me that no matter what pressure or change I face, I can maintain a professional and stable service spirit, which is why I believe I'm suited to be a cabin crew member.

articles.title: 平時休假喜歡做什麼？是否能適應輪班生活？
sentences: What do you like doing on days off?
Can you adapt to shift work?

articles.title: 平時休假喜歡做什麼？是否能適應輪班生活？
sentences: On days off, I enjoy learning Korean, exercising, and exploring new things — interests I can pursue even with an irregular schedule.
Having already worked shifts at the hotel, I'm used to adjusting my circadian rhythm and daily pace.

articles.title: 工作中最容易犯的小錯是什麼？
sentences: When handling multiple tasks at once, I've occasionally made small clerical errors, like entering the wrong date or room type.
I've since built a habit of double-checking, which has greatly reduced this kind of mistake.

articles.title: 你做事偏理性還是感性？為什麼？
sentences: Are you more rational or more emotional in how you work?
Why?

articles.title: 你做事偏理性還是感性？為什麼？
sentences: I consider myself a balance of both.
When facing a problem, I first analyze the situation and rules rationally, but when interacting with passengers, I bring empathy and emotional sensitivity.
I believe this balance is essential in service work.

articles.title: 你是注重細節的人，還是重視效率的人？
sentences: I believe both matter, but if I had to choose, I'd lean toward attention to detail, since in service industries small details often shape the overall passenger experience.
That said, I also plan processes in advance to maintain efficiency.

articles.title: 當主管或同事給你負面回饋時，你通常如何面對？
sentences: How do you usually respond when a supervisor or colleague gives you negative feedback?

articles.title: 當主管或同事給你負面回饋時，你通常如何面對？
sentences: I calmly listen to the feedback first, without rushing to defend myself, and reflect on what I can improve.
At the hotel, my supervisor once pointed out that I could handle a guest interaction more tactfully; I accepted it humbly and adjusted, which made my service more mature going forward.

articles.title: 你目前最需要提升的三項能力是什麼？
sentences: What are the three abilities you most need to strengthen right now?

articles.title: 你目前最需要提升的三項能力是什麼？
sentences: I believe I need to continue strengthening: first, fluency in spoken Korean; second, faster on-the-spot reactions in emergency situations; and third, mastery of professional English terminology, especially aviation-related vocabulary.

articles.title: 很多人認為空服員只是端茶倒水，你怎麼看？
sentences: Many people think cabin crew just serve drinks.
How do you respond to that?

articles.title: 很多人認為空服員只是端茶倒水，你怎麼看？
sentences: I think this is a common misunderstanding.
Cabin crew must pass rigorous safety training and serve as first responders in emergencies.
Serving drinks is only a small part of the job — the real core is ensuring passenger safety and emergency readiness.

articles.title: 為什麼選擇航空業，而不是其他服務業？
sentences: My background in hotel service and arts-center administration and marketing built a strong interest in both service and cross-cultural communication.
The airline industry is one of the few fields that combines these to the fullest — meeting passengers of different nationalities every day while requiring strong professionalism and safety awareness.
That's exactly what draws me from hospitality into aviation.

articles.title: 請分享你未來三年的職涯規劃。
sentences: In year one, I want to solidify my grasp of the company's service standards and safety procedures, quickly becoming familiar with different aircraft types and route-specific service details.
In year two, I want to further improve my language skills, especially Korean and English, to serve a wider range of routes.
In year three, I hope to have gained enough experience to move toward a senior cabin crew or training-related role, continuing to develop through ongoing professional education.

articles.title: 如果連續兩次航空公司面試都沒有錄取，你還會繼續努力嗎？
sentences: If you were unsuccessful at two airline interviews in a row, would you keep trying?

articles.title: 如果連續兩次航空公司面試都沒有錄取，你還會繼續努力嗎？
sentences: Yes.
I believe every interview is a learning opportunity.
Even if I'm unsuccessful twice in a row, I would analyze the reasons and keep adjusting, because becoming a cabin crew member has always been my clear goal.

articles.title: 如果另一半不喜歡你經常飛行或外站過夜，你會如何處理？
sentences: If your partner disliked your frequent flying and overnight layovers, how would you handle it?

articles.title: 如果另一半不喜歡你經常飛行或外站過夜，你會如何處理？
sentences: I would openly communicate with my partner about the nature and meaning of this job, and try to find a way of relating that works for both of us — for example, using days off for quality time together — so the relationship isn't negatively affected by the work schedule.

articles.title: 你期待的薪資待遇是多少？
sentences: I understand your airline has a clear salary structure for new cabin crew, so I would follow the company's standard starting salary and benefits.
What matters more to me is the training resources and long-term development opportunities the company provides.

articles.title: 你認為自己適合輪班與不固定作息嗎？
sentences: Yes, I believe I'm well suited to it.
Having already experienced shift work at the hotel, I know how to maintain energy and focus through regular exercise and diet.
I believe this experience will help me quickly adapt to a cabin crew schedule.

articles.title: 面對每天重複的安全檢查與服務流程，你如何保持熱情？
sentences: Facing the same safety checks and service routines every day, how do you stay engaged?

articles.title: 面對每天重複的安全檢查與服務流程，你如何保持熱情？
sentences: I remind myself that these repeated procedures are exactly what keeps passengers safe — every time I carry them out properly, I'm taking responsibility for their safety.
This sense of mission helps me stay passionate and focused.

articles.title: 請分享一件你曾經展現同理心的事情。
sentences: While working at the hotel, an elderly guest traveling alone became anxious due to a language barrier.
I slowed my speech, used simple English and body language to help him check in, and kept an eye on whether he needed further help afterward.
When he checked out, he specifically thanked me, saying my help made his trip much more reassuring.
This confirmed for me that genuine empathy can ease a passenger's worries.

articles.title: 你害怕搭飛機或高空嗎？
sentences: No, I'm not.
I feel excited and look forward to flying.
My past experience flying to Korea and Canada has also made me familiar and comfortable with the flight environment.

articles.title: 從學生或上班族轉換成全天候輪班的空服員，你做了哪些準備？
sentences: Moving from being a student or office worker to round-the-clock shift work — what have you done to prepare?

articles.title: 從學生或上班族轉換成全天候輪班的空服員，你做了哪些準備？
sentences: During my time at the hotel, I already experienced shift work and irregular schedules, learning how to manage sleep and energy.
I've also continued improving my language skills and physical fitness to prepare myself mentally and physically for intensive training and round-the-clock shift work.

articles.title: 請分享本航空公司近年的重要發展。
sentences: [Customize per airline] As I understand it, your airline has recently continued expanding its destinations, updating its fleet, and actively improving cabin service quality and digital experience, reflecting a focus on sustainability and passenger experience.

articles.title: 可以接受外派或異地基地嗎？
sentences: Would you accept an overseas posting or being based away from home?

articles.title: 可以接受外派或異地基地嗎？
sentences: Yes.
Having gone through an exchange in Korea and a study program in Canada, I have experience adapting to new environments and lifestyles.
I see being assigned overseas or to a different base as a good opportunity to broaden my horizons.

articles.title: 什麼是紅眼航班(Red-Eye Flight)？
sentences: A Red-Eye Flight is a flight that departs late at night and arrives early in the morning.
Passengers often sacrifice sleep by flying overnight, and it's also a challenge for crew members in terms of energy management and adjusting their schedules.

articles.title: 什麼是待命(Standby)、外站過夜以及臨時加班執勤？
sentences: Standby duty means a crew member must be ready to support flight scheduling at short notice; overnight layovers mean resting in the destination city after a flight before continuing duty the next day; and temporary overtime duty means accommodating additional flight assignments as scheduling requires.
All of these require flexibility as part of cabin crew work.

articles.title: 如果航班延誤、備降或取消，空服員的主要職責是什麼？
sentences: If a flight is delayed, diverted or cancelled, what are cabin crew's main responsibilities?

articles.title: 如果航班延誤、備降或取消，空服員的主要職責是什麼？
sentences: The cabin crew's main duty is to promptly and clearly inform passengers of the situation, help calm their emotions, and coordinate follow-up arrangements such as accommodation, connecting flights, or rebooking, ensuring passengers feel properly cared for throughout.

articles.title: 你認為航空業最重要的核心價值是什麼？
sentences: What do you consider the most important core value in the aviation industry?

articles.title: 你認為航空業最重要的核心價值是什麼？
sentences: I believe the most important core value in the airline industry is safety, followed by high-quality service experience.
Only when passenger and crew safety is ensured does service become meaningful.

articles.title: 民用航空可以分為哪些類型？
sentences: Civil aviation can be categorized into scheduled flights, charter flights, cargo airlines, and business/private aviation, each differing in operating model and target passengers.

articles.title: 機長、副機長、座艙長、空服員以及航空安全員的工作內容有什麼不同？
sentences: How do the roles of captain, first officer, purser, cabin crew and air marshal differ?

articles.title: 機長、副機長、座艙長、空服員以及航空安全員的工作內容有什麼不同？
sentences: The Captain is responsible for overall flight safety and final decisions; the First Officer assists the Captain in flight operations; the Cabin Manager oversees cabin service and crew management; cabin crew carry out cabin service and safety duties; and the air marshal/security officer specifically handles onboard security and threat response.

articles.title: 客艙內有哪些重要的緊急安全設備？
sentences: Important emergency safety equipment in the cabin includes oxygen masks, life vests, fire extinguishers, emergency lighting systems, evacuation slides, and first aid kits.
Cabin crew must be familiar with the location and use of each item to respond to various emergencies.

articles.title: 氧氣面罩、救生衣、滅火器及緊急照明設備的使用時機為何？
sentences: When are oxygen masks, life vests, fire extinguishers and emergency lighting used?

articles.title: 氧氣面罩、救生衣、滅火器及緊急照明設備的使用時機為何？
sentences: Oxygen masks are used when cabin pressure is lost; life vests are used for water landings; fire extinguishers are used in the event of an onboard fire; and emergency lighting is activated during power loss or evacuation to help passengers identify escape routes.

articles.title: 為什麼旅客不能隨意更換座位？
sentences: Seating arrangements affect the aircraft's weight balance and emergency evacuation planning, and emergency exit seats have specific eligibility requirements, so passengers cannot freely change seats, in order to ensure flight safety.

articles.title: 請說明液體、鋰電池及行動電源的攜帶規定。
sentences: Under aviation regulations, liquids over 100ml must be checked in; lithium batteries and power banks cannot be checked in and must be carried in the cabin, subject to watt-hour limits to avoid safety risks.

articles.title: 常見的特殊餐食有哪些？
sentences: Common special meals include vegetarian, Hindu, kosher, gluten-free, children's meals, and health-specific options like low-sodium or low-sugar meals, usually provided based on passengers' advance requests.

articles.title: 什麼是轉機、經停以及直飛航班？
sentences: What is the difference between a connecting flight, a stopover and a direct flight?

articles.title: 什麼是轉機、經停以及直飛航班？
sentences: A direct flight goes straight to the destination without landing en route; a stopover flight lands en route but passengers stay on the same aircraft; a connecting flight requires passengers to change to a different flight at an intermediate airport to reach their final destination.

articles.title: 高原機場航班有哪些需要注意的事項？
sentences: High-altitude airports have thinner air, making takeoff and landing conditions more demanding.
Crew must pay special attention to passengers' altitude sickness symptoms, such as dizziness or breathing difficulty, and ensure adequate onboard oxygen supply.

articles.title: 機上的急救設備由誰負責使用？
sentences: Onboard first aid equipment is generally used by trained cabin crew.
If a medical professional onboard volunteers to help, cabin crew will cooperate with them according to protocol.

articles.title: 疫情之後，航空服務有哪些改變？
sentences: After the pandemic, the airline industry placed greater emphasis on hygiene, such as enhanced cabin cleaning and disinfection and individually packaged meals and amenities, while also offering more flexible ticketing and rebooking policies to meet passengers' heightened need for safety and flexibility.

articles.title: 商務艙、豪華經濟艙與經濟艙的服務差異有哪些？
sentences: What are the service differences between business, premium economy and economy class?

articles.title: 商務艙、豪華經濟艙與經濟艙的服務差異有哪些？
sentences: Business class offers more spacious seating, refined dining, and personalized service; premium economy sits between the two, offering more seat space and better meals; economy class focuses on standardized service with relatively smaller seating.

articles.title: 如果旅客在機上吸菸，空服員應如何處理？
sentences: I'd stop them immediately, clearly explain that smoking is prohibited throughout the aircraft, and make sure the cigarette is properly extinguished — because fire in the cabin is one of the most dangerous situations there is.
I'd be firm without humiliating them, and if they continued I'd notify the purser to handle it under company procedure, handing it to the authorities after landing if necessary.
To me there's no room for discussion here: a safety rule is a rule.

articles.title: 為什麼飛機起飛與降落時需要打開遮光板？
sentences: Opening the window shades allows crew and passengers' eyes to adjust to outside light conditions in advance, so that if an emergency evacuation is needed, everyone can quickly assess the outside environment, ensuring a smooth evacuation.

articles.title: 遇到雷雨天繞飛時，你會如何向旅客說明？
sentences: When the aircraft deviates around a thunderstorm, how would you explain it to passengers?

articles.title: 遇到雷雨天繞飛時，你會如何向旅客說明？
sentences: I would calmly and clearly explain to passengers that, to ensure flight safety, the Captain has decided to adjust the route to avoid severe weather — a common and necessary safety measure — and ask them to stay calm and keep their seatbelts fastened.

articles.title: 長程跨時區航班中，如何兼顧旅客休息與客艙服務？
sentences: On long-haul flights across time zones, how do you balance passenger rest with cabin service?

articles.title: 長程跨時區航班中，如何兼顧旅客休息與客艙服務？
sentences: On long-haul, cross-timezone flights, I would arrange rest and service according to flight phases — for instance providing full service during meal and entertainment peak times, and dimming lights with quiet reminders to rest at night — balancing service quality with passengers' circadian rhythm adjustment.

articles.title: 請分享一次你在團隊中擔任重要角色的經驗。
sentences: Tell me about a time you played a key role in a team.

articles.title: 請分享一次你在團隊中擔任重要角色的經驗。
sentences: During my internship at the Xinzhuang Cultural and Arts Center, I coordinated venue setup and staffing for an exhibition opening, communicating simultaneously with the curatorial team, venue management, and marketing team to ensure a smooth event.
This taught me to balance multiple stakeholders' needs and proactively take on a coordinating role.

articles.title: 如果團隊成員能力差異很大，你會如何合作？
sentences: If team members have very different ability levels, how would you work together?

articles.title: 如果團隊成員能力差異很大，你會如何合作？
sentences: I would assign tasks based on each person's strengths, proactively help or guide in areas where someone is weaker, and remain patient and respectful, so the team can perform at its best overall.

articles.title: 如果資深空服員不願意配合新人工作，你會怎麼做？
sentences: If a senior crew member is unwilling to cooperate with a new colleague, what would you do?

articles.title: 如果資深空服員不願意配合新人工作，你會怎麼做？
sentences: I would show an eager-to-learn attitude and respect for senior colleagues' experience, proactively asking for guidance while reliably completing my own tasks to build trust, gradually earning more willingness to cooperate.

articles.title: 如果同事安全檢查做得不確實，你會怎麼處理？
sentences: If a colleague doesn't perform a safety check properly, how would you handle it?

articles.title: 如果同事安全檢查做得不確實，你會怎麼處理？
sentences: There's no room for personal courtesy in a safety check.
I'd remind them in the moment in a way that doesn't embarrass them — something like "shall I take another look at this row with you?" — covering the gap as support rather than criticism.
If they didn't accept it, or it happened again, I'd absolutely report it to the purser, because this concerns everyone on board, not the relationship between two colleagues.
My principle is simple: you can protect someone's dignity, but never safety.

articles.title: 如果兩位空服員在客艙發生爭執，你會如何處理？
sentences: If two crew members argue in the cabin, how would you handle it?

articles.title: 如果兩位空服員在客艙發生爭執，你會如何處理？
sentences: I would step in to de-escalate emotions immediately, preventing the dispute from escalating in front of passengers, then privately understand the cause afterward and help both parties communicate rationally, reporting to the Cabin Manager if needed.

articles.title: 你喜歡主動承擔工作，還是等待分配？
sentences: Do you prefer to take on work proactively, or wait to be assigned?

articles.title: 你喜歡主動承擔工作，還是等待分配？
sentences: I tend to take initiative.
At the hotel, I made it a habit to ask if help was needed after finishing my own tasks.
I believe this proactive attitude improves overall team efficiency.

articles.title: 如果你的工作量比其他同事多，你會如何調整心態？
sentences: If your workload is heavier than your colleagues', how would you adjust your mindset?

articles.title: 如果你的工作量比其他同事多，你會如何調整心態？
sentences: I would view it as an opportunity to gain experience and a sign of being trusted, focusing on doing my own work well rather than comparing myself to others, while also appropriately raising the workload distribution with my supervisor.

articles.title: 如果機長與客艙組員的意見不同，你會如何配合？
sentences: If the captain and the cabin crew disagree, how would you respond?

articles.title: 如果機長與客艙組員的意見不同，你會如何配合？
sentences: On decisions involving flight safety, I would follow the Captain's judgment as final, since the Captain has the most comprehensive view of the flight situation, while still respecting cabin crew suggestions as valuable input.

articles.title: 飛行前簡報時，你的工作習慣是什麼？
sentences: I arrive early and listen attentively to the briefing, carefully noting key information for the flight (such as special passengers or weather conditions), and proactively confirm my assigned area and responsibilities.

articles.title: 航班落地後，你如何完成工作交接？
sentences: I organize any special situations or pending matters from the flight clearly, and hand them over explicitly — verbally or in writing — to the next crew or ground staff, ensuring no information is missed.

articles.title: 你的溝通風格偏直接還是委婉？
sentences: I would describe my communication style as tactful yet clear.
I first try to understand the other person's position, then express my own views gently but directly, aiming to convey the message clearly while maintaining harmony.

articles.title: 面對情緒激動的人，你會如何安撫？
sentences: At the hotel, I once dealt with a guest upset because a flight delay disrupted their plans.
I calmly listened to their frustration, expressed understanding, then explained concretely what help I could offer — this usually effectively calms the person down.

articles.title: 如果自己覺得委屈，你會當下反駁還是事後溝通？
sentences: If you feel wronged, would you push back in the moment or address it afterwards?

articles.title: 如果自己覺得委屈，你會當下反駁還是事後溝通？
sentences: I would choose to address it afterward.
In the moment, I stay professional and focus on the task at hand, then rationally express my thoughts and feelings once emotions have settled.

articles.title: 與青少年旅客互動時，你會注意什麼？
sentences: I would use a relaxed yet polite tone when interacting with teenage passengers, respecting their views and independence, while paying attention to any special needs or emotional state.

sentences: If you can't communicate with a foreign passenger through language, what would you do?

articles.title: 如何做到態度親切，但立場堅定？

articles.title: 你容易受到他人的情緒影響嗎？
sentences: I believe I can empathize with others' emotions without being overly affected by them.
My hotel work trained me to stay calm and professional amid busy schedules and passengers in various emotional states — one reason I believe I'm suited to cabin crew work.

articles.title: 身邊的人一直抱怨工作，你會如何保持正向？
sentences: If those around you constantly complain about work, how do you stay positive?

articles.title: 身邊的人一直抱怨工作，你會如何保持正向？
sentences: I would listen to their feelings without letting the negativity affect me, reminding myself to focus on the meaning and growth opportunities in the work, staying positive.

articles.title: 如果旅客質疑你的專業能力，甚至公開質問你，你會怎麼回應？
sentences: If a passenger questions your competence, even publicly, how would you respond?

articles.title: 如果旅客質疑你的專業能力，甚至公開質問你，你會怎麼回應？
sentences: I would stay calm and respond to the passenger's doubts with professional, well-founded explanations.

articles.title: 如果兩位旅客搶同一個行李置物空間，你會如何協調？

articles.title: 如果兩位旅客搶同一個行李置物空間，你會如何協調？
sentences: I would help assess the luggage size and available space, coordinate moving some items to another bin, and calmly ease any tension between the two passengers.

articles.title: 如果座艙長當眾責備你，但你認為自己沒有錯，你會怎麼做？

articles.title: 如果座艙長當眾責備你，但你認為自己沒有錯，你會怎麼做？
sentences: In the moment I'd say "understood."
Order in the cabin and the team's authority matter more than whether I was right, and arguing in front of passengers only unsettles them.
After landing, or at an appropriate time, I'd explain my reasoning to the purser privately and ask them to guide me on the correct approach.
If it turns out I was wrong, I've learned something.
To me, complying first and discussing afterwards is the mature way to handle it within a team.

articles.title: 如果因文化差異讓旅客感到不舒服，你會如何化解？

articles.title: 如果因文化差異讓旅客感到不舒服，你會如何化解？
sentences: I would first understand the specific cause of discomfort, then explain the cultural background respectfully to both parties, aiming to resolve the discomfort in a neutral, considerate way without embarrassing anyone.

articles.title: 如果旅客因為小朋友吵鬧而發生爭執，你會怎麼處理？

articles.title: 如果長期合作的同事與你關係緊張，你會如何維持工作關係？

articles.title: 如果長期合作的同事與你關係緊張，你會如何維持工作關係？

articles.title: 在所有衝突情境中，你最重要的原則是什麼？
sentences: I believe the most important principle in any conflict situation is safety first, service second, staying calm and respectful toward all parties, and handling issues based on facts rather than emotional reactions.

articles.title: 旅客預訂素食餐，但航空公司沒有備到餐點，你會怎麼處理？

sentences: I would apologize immediately and check for alternative food options onboard (fruit, bread, or a vegetarian meal), while reporting the incident to help improve the catering process.

articles.title: 超大件行李放不進行李置物櫃，旅客拒絕托運，你會怎麼做？

articles.title: 超大件行李放不進行李置物櫃，旅客拒絕托運，你會怎麼做？
sentences: I would patiently explain safety regulations and space limitations, help find alternative storage, and if it still doesn't fit, sincerely explain that checking the bag is the only safe solution.

articles.title: 旅客擅自打開其他人的行李置物櫃，引發爭執，你會怎麼處理？

articles.title: 旅客擅自打開其他人的行李置物櫃，引發爭執，你會怎麼處理？
sentences: I would step in to calm both parties, confirm which bag belongs to whom, and help find alternative storage space, moving some luggage to another bin if necessary to resolve the dispute peacefully.

articles.title: 行李置物空間不足，你會如何協調？
sentences: I would coordinate overhead space across the cabin, helping passengers distribute luggage or suggesting smaller items go under the seat, balancing everyone's needs.

articles.title: 逃生出口座位旅客伸腳阻礙通道，你會怎麼勸導？

articles.title: 逃生出口座位旅客伸腳阻礙通道，你會怎麼勸導？
sentences: I would politely but firmly remind the passenger that the emergency exit aisle must remain clear for safe evacuation, and ask them to adjust their posture accordingly.

articles.title: 餐點不小心灑到旅客衣服上，你會怎麼辦？
sentences: You accidentally spill food on a passenger's clothes.
What would you do?

articles.title: 餐點不小心灑到旅客衣服上，你會怎麼辦？
sentences: I'd apologise sincerely straight away, hand them a damp towel to help immediately, and take the remaining drinks back to the galley to prevent a second accident.
Then I'd bring both dry and damp towels with soap and ask whether they'd like to use the lavatory to clean up, laying a blanket over the seat in the meantime.
Once they're back I'd check on them again and explain any follow-up cleaning or compensation under company policy.
To me, how fast and how genuinely you recover matters more than how many times you apologise.

articles.title: 同時有很多旅客按服務鈴，你會如何安排服務順序？
sentences: Several call bells ring at once.

articles.title: 同時有很多旅客按服務鈴，你會如何安排服務順序？
sentences: I would prioritize by urgency, handling health or safety-related needs first, then informing other passengers I'll be with them shortly and serving them as quickly as possible, ensuring everyone feels attended to.

articles.title: 毛毯數量不足，你會如何協調？
sentences: I would prioritize passengers with special needs (elderly, infants), explain the limited supply to others, and distribute them fairly and thoughtfully.

articles.title: 如何協助輪椅旅客完成登機與下機？
sentences: I would confirm the passenger's needs in advance, help them safely transfer to an onboard wheelchair or seat, and accompany them throughout boarding and deplaning to ensure safety and make them feel respected and well cared for.

articles.title: 如何照顧無人陪伴兒童(UM)？
sentences: I would pay special attention to this child's seating and needs, proactively check on their meals and emotional state, regularly check on their safety during the flight, and provide detailed handover information to ground staff or family upon arrival.

articles.title: 糖尿病旅客出現低血糖症狀，你會如何協助？

articles.title: 嬰兒一直哭鬧，家長手忙腳亂，你會怎麼協助？

articles.title: 嬰兒一直哭鬧，家長手忙腳亂，你會怎麼協助？
sentences: I would proactively offer help, providing warm water, a toy, or soothing suggestions, so the parent feels supported rather than overwhelmed.

articles.title: 剛開完刀的旅客感到傷口疼痛，你會如何安撫？

articles.title: 剛開完刀的旅客感到傷口疼痛，你會如何安撫？
sentences: I would ask about their pain level, help adjust their seat position for comfort, ask if they have their own pain medication, and notify the Cabin Manager for further help if needed.

articles.title: 同時有多位旅客身體不適，你會如何安排優先順序？

articles.title: 同時有多位旅客身體不適，你會如何安排優先順序？
sentences: I would prioritize by severity of symptoms — for example, passengers with breathing difficulty or reduced consciousness before those with milder discomfort — and quickly notify the Cabin Manager to coordinate additional help.

articles.title: 旅客要求使用自備醫療設備，但不符合規定，你會如何說明？

articles.title: 旅客要求使用自備醫療設備，但不符合規定，你會如何說明？
sentences: I would sincerely explain the company's safety regulations and limitations regarding personal medical equipment, and help find a compliant alternative, ensuring the passenger understands it's for flight safety.

articles.title: 航班因天候因素延誤三小時，旅客開始抱怨，你會如何安撫？

articles.title: 航班因天候因素延誤三小時，旅客開始抱怨，你會如何安撫？

articles.title: 航班備降其他機場，旅客情緒激動要求立即下機，你會如何處理？

articles.title: 深夜航班延誤導致旅客情緒失控，你會怎麼處理？

articles.title: 延誤期間，你會如何主動發布資訊降低旅客焦慮？

articles.title: 延誤期間，你會如何主動發布資訊降低旅客焦慮？
sentences: I would proactively make regular announcements with the latest updates, honestly informing passengers even without new developments, so they feel continuously cared for rather than left waiting.

articles.title: 旅客懷疑你翻動他的隨身物品，你會怎麼辦？

sentences: I would calmly and sincerely explain that I did not touch their belongings, and if needed, ask the Cabin Manager to help clarify, avoiding emotional arguments.

articles.title: 旅客因飛機顛簸而辱罵空服員，你會如何回應？

articles.title: 旅客因飛機顛簸而辱罵空服員，你會如何回應？
sentences: I would remain professional and calm, avoiding direct confrontation, first expressing understanding of their distress, then explaining that the measures taken during turbulence are necessary for safety, seeking help from the Cabin Manager if needed.

articles.title: 旅客在社群平台直播抱怨航空公司，你會如何保持專業？

sentences: I would maintain my usual professional service, not letting the livestream affect me, continuing to properly address the passenger's needs and concerns per protocol.

articles.title: 醉酒旅客大聲喧嘩並影響其他旅客，你會如何處理？

sentences: I would politely but firmly remind the passenger to lower their voice, assess whether alcohol service should be paused, and if the situation worsens, immediately notify the Cabin Manager and follow company SOPs.

articles.title: 醉酒旅客企圖闖入駕駛艙，你會怎麼做？

articles.title: 醉酒旅客搶奪機上餐具並揮舞，你會如何應變？

articles.title: 醉酒旅客搶奪機上餐具並揮舞，你會如何應變？
sentences: I would immediately keep a safe distance and notify the Cabin Manager and other crew, following trained procedures to de-escalate or restrain the passenger while ensuring everyone's safety.

articles.title: 醉酒旅客拿手機錄影並威脅投訴，你會如何保持專業？

articles.title: 醉酒旅客拿手機錄影並威脅投訴，你會如何保持專業？
sentences: I would remain professional and calm, not reacting emotionally to provocation, continuing to handle the situation properly per SOPs, and honestly documenting the incident to report to my supervisor afterward.

articles.title: 航班落地後需要移交相關單位處理，你會如何配合？
sentences: If a case must be handed to the authorities after landing, how would you assist?

articles.title: 航班落地後需要移交相關單位處理，你會如何配合？
sentences: I would accurately document the incident and cooperate with ground authorities and relevant personnel to complete the handover and follow-up process per company protocol.

articles.title: 你認為什麼情況下應該立即尋求其他機組員協助？
sentences: In what situations do you think you should immediately call for other crew members?

articles.title: 你認為什麼情況下應該立即尋求其他機組員協助？
sentences: When a situation involves passenger safety, a health emergency, or something I cannot properly handle alone, I would immediately seek help from other crew members or the Cabin Manager to ensure the issue is resolved quickly and correctly.

articles.title: 如果旅客聲稱自己攜帶爆裂物，你會如何處理？
sentences: If a passenger claims to be carrying explosives, how would you handle it?

articles.title: 如果旅客聲稱自己攜帶爆裂物，你會如何處理？

articles.title: 如果旅客偷偷將寵物藏在行李內帶上機，你會怎麼做？

articles.title: 如果旅客偷偷將寵物藏在行李內帶上機，你會怎麼做？
sentences: I would handle it per company policy, explain the relevant regulations, and help arrange next steps, ensuring other passengers' safety and comfort aren't affected.

articles.title: 如果發生劫機威脅，你會如何配合機組員處理？
sentences: This is the highest level of security incident.

articles.title: 如果發現疑似毒品或不明粉末，你會如何處理？
sentences: If you find suspected drugs or an unidentified powder, how would you handle it?

articles.title: 如果發現疑似毒品或不明粉末，你會如何處理？
sentences: I would avoid direct contact, immediately notify the Cabin Manager and Captain, and follow protocol for isolation and reporting to ensure onboard safety.

articles.title: 緊急出口座位旅客故意玩弄出口裝置，你會如何處理？

articles.title: 緊急出口座位旅客故意玩弄出口裝置，你會如何處理？

articles.title: 如果團體旅客中有人情緒激動，你會如何觀察與預防？
sentences: If someone in a tour group becomes agitated, how would you observe and prevent escalation?

articles.title: 如果團體旅客中有人情緒激動，你會如何觀察與預防？
sentences: I would continuously observe the passenger's words and behavior, check in on them appropriately, and notify the Cabin Manager in advance to prevent escalation.

articles.title: 飛機遇到強烈亂流時，你最重要的工作是什麼？
sentences: The most important thing is securing my own safety first, because an injured crew member can't help anyone.
I'd get to the nearest seat and fasten the belt, or hold onto a fixed handhold.
At the same time I'd use a clear, steady voice to tell passengers to fasten their seatbelts and stay seated, assisting anyone not yet seated only if it's safe to do so.
Once it passes, I'd check the cabin for injuries.
To me, in a moment like that the crew's composure is itself the most effective reassurance.

articles.title: 夜間長程航班如何兼顧旅客休息與安全巡視？
sentences: On overnight long-haul flights, how do you balance passenger rest with safety checks?

articles.title: 夜間長程航班如何兼顧旅客休息與安全巡視？
sentences: I would minimize noise and light disturbance during checks, patrolling the cabin quietly at regular intervals, balancing passenger rest with flight safety.

articles.title: 如果機上洗手間發生火警，你會如何處理？
sentences: If a fire breaks out in a lavatory, how would you handle it?

articles.title: 如果機上洗手間發生火警，你會如何處理？
sentences: I would immediately use the fire extinguisher to put out the fire and notify the Captain and Cabin Manager, guiding nearby passengers away from the area to ensure safety.

articles.title: 行李置物櫃內的行動電源起火，你會如何處理？
sentences: A power bank catches fire inside an overhead bin.
How would you handle it?

articles.title: 行李置物櫃內的行動電源起火，你會如何處理？
sentences: I would immediately use the fire extinguisher on the burning power bank, isolate the area per trained procedure, and notify the Captain and Cabin Manager for further action.

articles.title: 客艙出現煙霧，你會如何引導旅客？
sentences: I would immediately notify the Captain and Cabin Manager, follow trained procedures to identify the smoke's source and take firefighting or risk-mitigation actions, while guiding passengers to stay calm and prepare for further action if needed.

articles.title: 如果機長宣布緊急撤離，你的工作是什麼？
sentences: My job is to direct passengers out quickly and in an orderly way, following my training.
I'd first confirm the exterior of my assigned exit is safe and usable, then repeat short, clear commands — "release seatbelts, leave everything, come this way."
I'd prioritise passengers with reduced mobility and firmly stop anyone trying to take baggage.
I'd only leave once I've confirmed the cabin is clear.
To me, the critical thing in an evacuation is consistent commands, so passengers have no room to hesitate.

articles.title: 老人、小孩與孕婦的撤離協助重點為何？
sentences: What are the key points when helping elderly passengers, children and pregnant women evacuate?

articles.title: 老人、小孩與孕婦的撤離協助重點為何？
sentences: During evacuation, priority should be given to helping the elderly, children, and pregnant passengers reach the evacuation slide safely and use it correctly, paying attention to any need for extra support or guidance to avoid falls or delays.

articles.title: 如果發生水上迫降，你會如何協助旅客？
sentences: I would help passengers properly put on their life vests, guide them to the exits to use life rafts or slides, and keep the evacuation calm and orderly.

articles.title: 發動機故障造成旅客恐慌，你會如何安撫？

articles.title: 發動機故障造成旅客恐慌，你會如何安撫？
sentences: I would calmly and professionally explain that the crew is following procedures to address the issue, continuing to provide reassuring information to prevent panic from spreading.

articles.title: 客艙失壓且氧氣面罩掉落，你會如何處理？
sentences: I would immediately instruct passengers to put on their oxygen masks, demonstrate correct usage, help passengers with reduced mobility or children put theirs on, and follow the Captain's instructions for further action.

North America had seven, and the newest is Phoenix, launched in December 2025 as the first nonstop from Asia, serving business demand from the semiconductor supply chain.
The fleet is around 68 aircraft, led by A350s, A330s and 777-300ERs.
To me, the Phoenix route best shows how China Airlines follows Taiwan's industries.

articles.title: __QUESTION_BANK__ 274
sentences: Flight attendants serve as the primary brand ambassadors.
I believe that providing personalized and thoughtful service is crucial.
By anticipating guests' needs and delivering tailored experiences, we can directly contribute to maintaining and elevating Cathay Pacific's reputation for exceptional global service.

articles.title: __QUESTION_BANK__ 274
sentences: I see cabin crew as the only company representative a passenger spends extended time with at close range.

Passengers may not remember whether the booking system was easy to use, but they will remember whether someone treated them well on that flight — so every action a crew member takes is quietly defining the brand.

That matters even more at China Airlines, because it's Taiwan's oldest national carrier with the plum blossom on the tail, and many foreign passengers form their impression of Taiwan through that one flight.
There's a line I hold onto: the uniform is a badge of honour, not something to show off.
In practice that means two things.
First, consistency between what I say and do — when I put on the uniform I'm not representing myself.
Second, self-discipline on social media; I wouldn't post about my duties or passengers to attract attention.
Protecting reputation isn't about handling a PR crisis well; it's about every flight ending without incident and with someone feeling looked after.

articles.title: __QUESTION_BANK__ 274
sentences: The STARLUX brand is built from details, and almost all of those details happen in the cabin — the lighting, the scent, how tableware is placed.
All of it ultimately depends on crew executing it in the moment.
A design can be planned to perfection, but what a passenger actually feels is the second something is handed to them.
So I see crew not as merely protecting the image, but as the final mile of the image itself.
For a young airline still building its reputation that responsibility is heavier: one unprofessional interaction can cancel out everything the company invested in experience design.
Practically I'd watch two things.
First, steadiness — my mood and service quality can't fluctuate with fatigue or a passenger's attitude, because passengers don't know how many sectors I've flown today.
Second, boundaries — in uniform I am STARLUX, not myself, and the same applies online; I wouldn't trade work content for attention.

articles.title: __QUESTION_BANK__ 274
sentences: For EVA, I think crew protect more than a service image — they protect a reputation for being safe and trustworthy.
EVA has held its SKYTRAX five-star rating and its place among the world's safest airlines not through publicity but because every crew member follows SOP on every flight.
Reputation accumulates slowly and collapses quickly: ten thousand flights done right never make the news, one incident does.

So I see following procedure as the most direct way to protect the brand, including when a passenger doesn't understand a rule or finds it inconvenient — I'd enforce it firmly but politely, because that is precisely why passengers trust EVA.
The other part is personal boundaries; wearing the green uniform means representing the company, so I wouldn't post anything about flights or passengers on social media.
Protecting reputation isn't an extra duty to me — it's doing the job properly, every single time.

articles.title: __QUESTION_BANK__ 275
sentences: China Airlines' brand spirit is hospitality built on putting the customer first, and I'd describe its warmth as making travel more meaningful.

Its identity is the plum blossom tail, with the blossom standing for the Taiwanese spirit, alongside the Mikado pheasant and blue magpie liveries, the pangolin conservation project, and sustainability work that leads much of Asia, such as SAF and plastic reduction.
The line I identify with most is making travel more meaningful, because it sets the goal of service higher than completing a procedure.
Travel is already an experience people remember; what we can decide is whether they remember inconvenience or the feeling of being cared for.
My proudest moment at Hyatt was helping a Colombian guest through an online check-in that only had a Chinese interface — it wasn't part of my job, but he came back the next day to thank me.
That taught me the meaningful part comes from the extra step.

articles.title: __QUESTION_BANK__ 275
sentences: STARLUX positions itself as a boutique airline, built on designing every flight as one complete experience — from cabin lighting, scent and uniforms to the inflight magazine kiânn, a name taken from the Taiwanese word for travel, which shows its cultural care in the naming alone.
I'd summarise its service keywords as three things: detail, anticipation, and a calm kind of warmth.
The one I identify with most is anticipation, because genuinely good service doesn't wait for a passenger to speak — it notices before they do.
While working the Hyatt front desk I noticed a pregnant guest standing uncomfortably in the queue, so I checked her in first and moved her to a room near the lift.
She said she hadn't expected anyone to notice.
That was when I understood that reassurance never comes from polished phrases; it comes from actually paying attention.
That's also where I think I fit STARLUX best.

articles.title: __QUESTION_BANK__ 275
sentences: EVA's corporate spirit is safe and efficient flight operations, warm and attentive service, and innovative, efficient management — and I think the order itself is the answer, because safety is written first.

On brand, EVA is a SKYTRAX five-star airline and a long-standing member of the world's safest carriers, with the Royal Laurel cabin representing its premium long-haul service and the Hello Kitty liveries giving a strictly disciplined company a genuinely approachable side.

The part I identify with most is that first phrase, flight safety, because service can run on warmth and instinct while safety runs only on systems and discipline — that is where the real professionalism of this job lies.
I studied Public Administration and Policy, four years of understanding why rules are written as they are and why shortcuts aren't acceptable.
At the hotel, one data-entry error led me to build the habit of reading every record back to confirm it.
I believe EVA's five-star rating isn't marketing; it's earned by every crew member following procedure on every flight, and that's who I want to be.
